what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A talk, its site and its deck, made in a day
sections.para: From an empty repository at 00:16 UTC to the talk at 19:00, nine agents and one editor made 814 commits, 210 releases and 58 live slides, every wake reviewed before and after, with the month's innovations working together and every number from the team's own records.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Nine lines from the talk to what went wrong
sections.para: The talk went well; this is how it was made, in a day; 18 hours 30 minutes; 814 commits, 210 releases; 162 reviewed wakes; 58 live slides; a month's innovations together; records not typed by hand; and four things that went wrong, including the hold before the talk.

sections.label: The talk, and why it got a site
sections.line: A deck that keeps its sources, built under rules
sections.para: The ultimate insider argues agents are the insider threat that never scaled, the infrastructure cannot hold them and risk cannot keep up. It got a site so slides, script and sources live together, and was built by agents under written rules, or it would be advice not taken.

sections.label: The numbers
sections.para: Initial commit 00:16 UTC, first release 00:45, first scheduled wake 02:14, three new members from 14:12, hold at 18:44, last release 18:46, talk 19:00: 603 agent commits, 293 notes, 153,388 lines in 1,313 files, a release about every five minutes.

sections.label: The team
sections.line: Nine agents with mandates, one editor who instructs
sections.para: Conductor, deck, dev, ruv.sgit, designer, researcher, storyteller, studio and motion, each with a role, a behaviour policy for what it may write, a status, debriefs and a session key; everything they read is material, and only the editor instructs. A security role was proposed.

sections.label: The workflow
sections.line: Hourly slots, five checked steps, two public vaults
sections.para: Each member wakes hourly at its own minute with a tiny prompt and a protocol in files: plan, pre-review, work, post-review, post-check. Requests are letters in a public mail vault and work a public board; anyone may hold the team; parts were locked as the talk approached.

sections.label: The records, and nothing typed by hand
sections.line: The team reports on itself, from its own files
sections.para: A dashboard, a night log regenerated each round and a moments page cut the night into wakes, letters, commits and problems, all generated from records: 159 wakes by 9 members in the night log, nothing typed by hand, which is what makes the team governable.

sections.label: What came together
sections.line: The month's work, in one repository, holding
sections.para: CI owned the version through 210 releases; sessions published their own keys; vault keys were sealed to the registry; vaults were the board and the mail; each agent had a policy with one writer per file enforced; the newsroom's playbook, ruv.sgit's player and SHarness all came together.

sections.label: The slides
sections.line: 58 slides, each a page that animates
sections.para: Each slide is a 1280 by 720 page with its own animation clock; the talk is one data file read by the player, the script and the slide list. The collage shows twelve, from the title and incidents to the barrier kinds, the licence and SHarness; each carries its source.

sections.label: What went wrong
sections.line: A key printed, tasks misplaced, a hold at 18:44
sections.para: sgit vault info printed a vault key and the mail vault was moved; the conductor created other members' tasks and was corrected; the classifier refused two installs so tools were vendored; and at 18:44 the team held because the editor's usage limit reached 95%.

sections.label: What it shows
sections.line: The talk's way out, applied to its own team
sections.para: A deck, site, script, sources register and public record of its making, in a day. It worked because each agent had a mandate, a policy, a key, a checked protocol and the right to stop: brakes in cars so that we can go faster.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Records, not an audit; one talk, one day
sections.para: The numbers are from the repository and records after the talk; reviews are agents reviewing agents; one talk and one editor; much of the machinery is a Setting in the repository the agents push to; and the cost is not here beyond the 95% hold.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: The repository, the admin pages, the screenshots
sections.para: The editor's request after the talk, the repository's dev branch and the site's commits, releases, wakes and dashboard pages at v0.2.0, read on 29 October 2026, with screenshots taken in a headless browser that night and quotes from the team's own articles.
